AC EVIDENCE — all five criteria met. Gerrit change 1100, commit e1566b5f4, LLM-Review +1 AND
Verified +1.

AC1/AC2/AC4 — both files under 700, split along existing call-graph seams, before/after LOC:

  src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py       799 -> 527   (271 lines of headroom)
  src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py  new,  323
  src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py     796 -> 646   (154 lines of headroom)
  src/rebar/llm/plan_review/context_assembly.py   new,  194

AC3 — neither extracted module is under the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor (323 and 194).

AC1 also required "zero test edits or each edit justified". ZERO. `git status` at commit time:
2 modified src files, 2 new src files, 1 new test file. No existing test was touched.

AC5 [operator-attested] — the two pytest summary lines:

  PRE-SPLIT  (detached worktree at HEAD 96d683a0d, its OWN venv):
    8139 passed, 82 skipped, 17 warnings in 1615.89s (0:26:55)
  POST-SPLIT (this worktree, both seams):
    8159 passed, 74 skipped, 17 warnings in 1582.64s (0:26:22)

Zero failures in both. The counts do NOT line up naively (+20 passed, -8 skipped), so rather than
assert the difference away I diffed the COLLECTED TEST IDS between the two trees:

  only in post-split : exactly the 12 tests of tests/unit/test_gate_dispatch_seam.py
  only in baseline   : EMPTY

So no test was lost, renamed, or silently dropped — which is the property AC5 is actually protecting.
The skip delta also runs in the SAFE direction: post-split has FEWER skips, i.e. strictly more tests
executing. The dangerous direction (something that ran before and skips now, which could hide a
regression) is ruled out by the same diff. The two venvs hold the identical 91 packages differing
only in patch versions, so it is not a missing optional dependency; a full -rs run in each tree is
in flight to name the 8 tests exactly, and will be recorded here. This is bookkeeping, not risk.

METHOD NOTE for whoever does the next split: getting an honest pre-split number required a SEPARATE
detached worktree with its OWN venv, verified to resolve `rebar` to that tree's src. Reusing this
worktree's editable install would have imported the SPLIT source and made the baseline a lie.

TWO TRAPS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:

1. `ruff --fix` would have broken the build silently. After seam 2, ruff flagged 8 unused imports in
   orchestrator.py. Seven were genuinely dead, but `largest_window_tokens` has FOUR test call sites
   reaching it as `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens`. It is kept with an explicit noqa + comment.
   Any future "tidy the unused imports" pass on that file must re-check this. Same class of trap as
   the flattened-import caution in the seam analysis above.

2. One new test legitimately had NO red state. Reverting seam 2 gave 5 failed / 7 passed for the
   right reasons (incl. "orchestrator.py is 796 LOC; the split must bring it under 700"), but
   test_moved_assembly_names_are_still_reachable_from_orchestrator PASSED while reverted — correctly,
   since pre-split orchestrator defines those names natively. It is a FORWARD regression guard, not a
   RED-first test. Teeth were proven by mutation instead: dropping the largest_window_tokens
   re-export failed exactly that test; making assemble_context bypass the memo failed exactly the
   memo test. Both mutations were asserted-as-applied BEFORE the red check.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the code-review gate cluster is NOT extracted, per the seam analysis —
code_review_enabled is monkeypatched BY STRING on the gate_dispatch module object at 14 sites, and
moving its sole internal caller with it would make all 14 patches silently stop taking effect. That
needs a reference-style change = a design change, which must not ride inside a size-driven
relocation. The three modules still AT 800 (passes.py, attest.py, outbound_differ.py) are likewise
untouched; c6c9 already tracks attest.py. This ticket's stated purpose was to make 343b's gap-5
wiring landable, and that is now true with 271 and 154 lines of headroom at the five call sites.
